sum: Home Depot shares have seen mixed momentum, with a sharp 20.9% rise over the past month but a small decline over the past week. This puts fresh focus on whether the current market price lines up with the cash the business can generate. Investors now face a simple question: Do the stock's cash flows support where the market has taken it?

Over the past 3 years, Home Depot has delivered a total return of 23.1%, which makes the link between its share price and its underlying cash generation more important for anyone thinking about what happens next.

Recent political developments that supported housing related companies and pushed Home Depot sharply higher may shape expectations for future demand, which can feed directly into the timing and durability of the retailer's cash flows.
The issue now is whether the current US$351.31 share price is justified by Home Depot's cash flows when viewed through a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate of intrinsic value.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach here focuses on the cash Home Depot can return to shareholders over time. Over the latest twelve months, the retailer generated roughly $15.2b in free cash flow, and the model extends that stream out with a 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity framework that tapers growth gradually over the coming decade.

Those projections assume Home Depot keeps producing sizeable, positive free cash flow rather than swinging between gains and losses, which is consistent with a mature, cash generative retailer. Even so, the DCF output sits meaningfully below the current $351.31 share price. This suggests the recent rally has pushed expectations ahead of what these projected cash flows imply. Because the post election surge in housing related stocks has already lifted sentiment and the share price, the model points to a market that is pricing in a lot of good news on future demand. Apple, Home Depot and GE Vernova Object to ICE-OKX Tokenized Stock Venue as Count Hits 59
sum: Apple, The Home Depot and GE Vernova have objected to having tokenized versions of their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, the planned onchain stock venue owned by Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and OKX, according to a public notice the venue dated Nov. 3.

The notice names 59 issuers that have sent it a notice of issuer objection. By Unchained's count of the venue's earlier filings, that compares with 56 in the Nov. 2 notice and 50 in the Oct. 30 notice, and no company has been removed from the list in that time. Like the earlier versions, the Nov. 3 filing does not say why any company objected, and it sets no date for trading to begin.

On Nov. 2, citing the 50 objectors in the Oct. 30 notice, Zero Knowledge Group founder Austin Campbell said on Unchained's Bits + Bips that "people are just objecting as soon as they find out about this thing." Lumida Wealth founder Ram Ahluwalia said on the same episode, "I don't know what's being solved by tokenizing a stock on chain."
The three new names join a roster that already included Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Tesla, Amazon and SpaceX.

The notice says the venue may list stocks tokenized by their issuer or by a third party unaffiliated with the issuer. An objection keeps third-party tokens of that company's shares off the venue. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs the joint venture, told reporters on Oct. 29 that objections now come in on a rolling basis. "The start period has passed. There's no end period," he said.

OKXICE LLC, a Texas company that ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc. own in equal halves, runs the venue under the SEC exemption for tokenized securities venues, published in the Federal Register on Sept. 22. Trades will settle in permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on XLayer, and only wallets holding a soulbound token issued by the venue can use them.

The notice states that the venue is "not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission" for this activity and has no policies addressing maximal extractable value. Its hook contract is to be audited by OKX Technology Inc. and by Certified Kernel Tech LLC before operations start.

What Is The True Hidden Price Of Home Depot Stock?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Home Depot (HD) trades at 22.3 times its last twelve months of adjusted earnings (normalized net income plus after-tax stock pay). That is a steep price for a company reporting less profit than it did four years ago. You pay for future profit, however, making it useful to weigh this price against expected profit for the next two fiscal years. So what does that same price buy on the profit ahead?

Based on the consensus forecast, Home Depot trades at 21.9 times expected profit for fiscal 2027, the year now under way, and 20.7 times expected profit for fiscal 2028. (Years here are named for the calendar year in which they end, meaning the period Home Depot refers to as fiscal 2026 is fiscal 2027 here.) This indicates the hidden price of Home Depot stock is still more than 20 times profit, whether you count the last twelve months or either forecast year.

For those multiples to be what you actually pay, Home Depot must grow sales near the top of its guidance and slightly widen its margin. The consensus forecast puts fiscal 2027 sales at $172 billion, up from $165 billion in fiscal 2026. That represents growth of about 4%, approaching the high end of the 2.5% to 4.5% range management guided in August for the same year.

For fiscal 2028, the forecast calls for sales to grow another 3.4%, outpacing the 2.5% rate Home Depot delivered over the last twelve months. While total sales rose 5.7% in the latest quarter, comparable sales increased only 1.7%. Recession-Proof Stocks: Industries That Thrive During Recessions
sum: The economy isn't recession-proof. It often follows a fairly predictable, if irregular, pattern known as the economic cycle. Periods of expansion can last for years before hitting a peak. What follows is a period of contraction -- a recession -- before the economy enters a trough ahead of the next expansion.

Recessionary periods can be brutal for investors. Stock market corrections and bear markets commonly occur during the contraction phase. Cyclical stocks -- companies in industries highly sensitive to the economic cycle -- are often the hardest hit during a recession.

However, some stock market sectors are more immune to the changes in the economic cycle. They offer investors somewhat recession-proof stocks to hold when economic turbulence arises. In fact, many companies in these sectors have increased their dividends every year for the past few decades, which included several notable recessions.
Here's a closer look at where to invest if you're worried that the economy is about to hit a rough patch.

Lower interest rates also make it more affordable to fund do-it-yourself home improvement projects and are generally good for economic growth -- benefiting the commercial and industrial customers.

sum: "You can do it. We can help." So goes the advertising slogan of Home Depot (HD -0.69%).

The company announced third-quarter financial results on Tuesday morning, and they were somewhat dire.

Revenue rose slightly, up 2.8% from a year earlier to $41.4 billion, in line with expectations. But adjusted diluted earnings were $3.74 per share -- $0.04 below the same period a year ago, and $0.10 below what Wall Street was looking for.

Management blamed a lack of storms in the quarter. Sales of storm recovery and repair items like generators and roofing are a big revenue category for the retailer. It also pointed to ongoing uncertainty and pressure in the U.S. housing market that is affecting home improvement demand.

Perhaps more ominously, the company cut its full-year earnings guidance. It now expects diluted earnings per share to decline 5% in 2025 compared to 2024. That's lower than its previous forecast of a 2% decline.

The sluggish U.S. housing market continues to be a major drag on the financial results of Home Depot and other home improvement retailers. They're highly dependent on sales to homeowners who are selling homes, as well as those who just purchased one.
